title: Italian musicians Gino and Cesario
summary: He describes his Italian bandmates and their meals in Bologna.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I see. Okay, you didn't speak any Italian but nevertheless how did the people of Italy react to the music and also to yourself?

Yeah, well you know music is the common language in all nationalities and there were two members of the Italian guys, one's name was Gino, he was a guitar player and another guy was the second trombone player by the name of Cesario and they called him Caesar for short and I wrote my solo -- it kind of appealed to him, I think he's still got it. And Gino, every time we hit a town, Gino would always look for me, "You go with me, let's go to bordello." He always looked for me to stay near me at the hotels and he'd say, "You go with me for bongai."

I'd go with him if he goes to -- in Bologna, that was a great place for Italian wine and hot stuff and wine and Italian bread and Italian cheese. We'd take it up to the hotel and put two tables together and we had a ball by ourselves, just Gino and I, we put on the bag. I was sorry to leave Italy because I formed a lot of nice acquaintances there. They were great people.
